authoring_channel: delegated coding agent; not vendor CLI or harness run
brief: Early-morning garden workbench with a ceramic mug giving off subtle backlit steam, a birch framing one side, a planted stone terrace and restrained natural materials. Prioritize a convincing scene and readable motion over a feature grid.
modifications: Rebuilt the bench and mug to real dimensions (about 1.45 m by 0.54 m and 0.85 m high; mug about 9 cm wide), with weathered wood and procedural stone, soil, clay and foliage materials.
Varied the planted pots and terrace stone courses, added mortar gaps and small joinery and wear details, and reframed the close view to keep the steam near the cup against garden structure.
Rendered successive review iterations, inspected the wide and close views, and tuned the steam volume and backlight for visible motion while preserving the small mug scale.
Batched repeated plants, stones and small path details with InstancedMesh after census review to keep the scene compact.

testing.result: 9 authored-camera GPU frames rendered; zero console errors, shader errors, update errors or host warnings. Scene census: 1,161,394 triangles, 133 meshes, 14,897 instances and 40 materials.
testing.staging: Temporary workspace contains a copy of this scene and a frozen copy of the shipped scene_threejs src/lib modules.

library_usability_notes: At real cup scale, makeSteam is a soft, low-contrast volume against an open dawn sky; the close view, dark garden backing and tuned local backlight are needed to make its motion apparent.
The steam volume has no opaque-scene depth integration, so avoid intersecting geometry and overlapping transparent volumes.
visual_limitations: The scene remains a stylized procedural garden. The steam reads as a soft, backlit wisp in the close view and is subtle in the wide establishing shot.
